title: A chained model starts from noticing
statement: Start a modelled think-aloud that chains procedures by noticing something in the text and wondering about it, then work the procedures to answer that self-posed question.
detail: The Grade 3 reading curriculum's procedure spec, quoted verbatim in the reading course renderer, says a modelling moment that chains procedures is not usually triggered by a question put to the one modelling: they notice something specific in the text, pose themselves a question about it, then work through the procedures to answer it (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, lines 685-695). The same spec runs the search for evidence inside the think-aloud, after the procedure's first step, because a reader does not find before they have a question (line 838). Both are design rules; nothing measured their effect.

evidence.quote: Chains are not usually triggered by a question posed to the teacher. The teacher notices something in the text and wonders about it, then works through the procedures to answer their own self-question.
Wonder - the teacher poses a question to themselves about it.
A reader does not "find" before they have a question: the search runs inside the think-aloud, immediately after the procedure's Step 1.
